transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything at once. My marriage, whether I’m falling behind at work, bills, house projects I keep not finishing… and I keep thinking I’m failing as a husband and a father.
How long have you been feeling this way—has this constant worrying been going on for weeks, or has it been present for six months or more?
About nine months now. It really started when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and the arguments at home started becoming more regular.
When you're worrying about these things—your marriage, work, bills—do you find it hard to stop or control the worry even when you try to set it aside?

Yeah, it’s really hard to stop. I’ll try to focus on the code in front of me, or even just breathe through a workout, but one worry leads to another. Before I know it, I’m twenty steps ahead—thinking a bad review means losing my job, and then my family is worse off because of me.
Along with the worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, fatigue, or trouble sleeping?

Yeah. I feel wound tight almost all day—like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. I catch myself pacing between meetings, and at chess club I’ll be tapping the pieces because sitting still feels almost impossible.
Besides the worry and tension, have you also been feeling down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. Mostly it feels like I’m just constantly stressed and worried, more than sad.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things that have nothing to do with the work situation or your marriage—like your health, world events, or other everyday matters?

Yeah—it's not just work or my marriage. It feels like everything piles on at once: bills, the house projects I keep not getting done, and whether I'm failing my family somehow. I can't seem to shut any of it off.
